title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, and roadmap
author: Elena Kim
content:
Summary:
This page is the canonical platform engineering playbook for Redwood Inference: it consolidates the authoritative systems & services inventory, how-tos for common platform tasks, the dashboards and alerting standards we operate to, immediate runbooks for P1/P2 incidents, a short retrospective summary of major reliability items from Q4 2025, and the roadmap for platform initiatives across Q1-Q3 2026. Owners and runbook contacts are listed alongside each item. Treat this as the single source of truth for operational procedures and as the checklist used during incident response and postmortem activities.

1) Overview
- Purpose: Provide a single, operationally-focused reference for platform systems and services (control plane, routing, deployment agents, observability pipeline, autoscaler, capacity manager, and CI/CD hooks).
- Scope: Hosted API runtime orchestration, Dedicated capacity orchestration, Private deployment control-plane components, platform infra (k8s clusters, cluster-autoscaler), observability, and the developer-facing platform services (deploy API, service registry, feature flags).
- Primary SLAs and SLOs (for platform services):
  - Control plane API: availability SLO 99.95% monthly, p99 latency < 200ms for small payloads (<1KB)
  - Deployment pipeline (build -> canary): median time-to-deploy 8m, failure rate < 1% per change window
  - Observability pipeline (metrics + tracing ingestion): ingestion latency < 2 min 95%
  - Alert notification: page routing latency < 30s for P1 alerts

2) Systems & Services inventory (owner, primary alert, runbook link)
| Service | Responsibility | Primary owner | Key SLO | Runbook |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| control-plane-api | API for model routing and customer config | Platform API Team | 99.95% | /runbooks/control-plane-api-incident |
| autoscaler | scales Dedicated pools and k8s nodes | Platform SRE | target p95 decision latency < 45s | /runbooks/autoscaler-failure |
| deployment-service | handles deploys, canaries, rollbacks | CI/CD Team | median deploy time < 8m | /runbooks/deployment-failure |
| observability-pipeline | metrics/traces/event ingestion | Observability Team | ingestion latency < 2m | /runbooks/observability-backfill |
| service-registry | service discovery for platform services | Platform Infra | 99.9% | /runbooks/service-registry |
| feature-flag-service | rollout control for experiments | Feature Flags Team | 99.9% | /runbooks/feature-flag-issues |

3) How-to: Add a new platform service (step-by-step)
Follow these steps when introducing a new service that will run on platform clusters and integrate with observability and alerting.
1. Design & Review
   - Create an ADR in /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records that includes API surface, performance expectations, and failure modes.
   - Add an entry to the systems inventory (contact Platform Docs owner).
2. Deploy scaffolding
   - Create k8s manifests and Terraform module. Follow infra-standards: use Resource Requests/Limits, PodDisruptionBudgets, and liveness/readiness probes. Example CPU/memory: requests: cpu: "200m", memory: "256Mi"; limits: cpu: "1000m", memory: "2Gi".
3. Observability integration
   - Add Prometheus metrics (request_count, error_count, request_latency_seconds bucketed).
   - Add structured logs (json with fields service, component, request_id, user_id).
   - Add OpenTelemetry spans for downstream calls.
4. Alerting & Dashboards
   - Add alert rules (see alerting standards below). Create a per-service dashboard (latency, errors, saturation).
5. Runbook & Ownership
   - Create a runbook stub in /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks and assign on-call owner.
6. Canary & Rollout
   - Add a canary pipeline in deployment-service: start at 1% traffic for 5m, monitor errors and latency for 10m before increasing.

CLI snippets:
- Create k8s resources: kubectl apply -f k8s/service.yaml --context=platform-qa
- Terraform plan/apply (example):
  terraform init
  terraform plan -var-file=env/qa.tfvars
  terraform apply -var-file=env/qa.tfvars

4) Dashboards & Alerts (standards)
Dashboards:
- Every platform service MUST have a dashboard with the following tiles: availability (success rate), p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate, error rate, CPU/memory saturation, and a top-10 slow endpoints list.
- Dashboard naming convention: platform.<service-name>.overview
- Dashboard owner annotation: add 'owner: team-name' in the dashboard metadata.

Alerting standards (severity, trigger, paging rules):
- P1 (page immediately to on-call):
  - Control plane API error rate > 5% over 3m AND p99 latency > 1s over 3m.
  - Autoscaler failing to reconcile > 3 consecutive cycles.
  - Observability pipeline ingestion failure > 10m.
- P2 (notify Slack #platform-alerts and email on-call):
  - Error rate > 2% for 10m.
  - Median latency regression > 50% vs baseline for 15m.
- P3 (ticket in tracker, no immediate page):
  - Single-host disk pressure, single instance 5xx spike < 10m.

Paging rules:
- PagerDuty escalation: 0 -> 5m (primary), 5 -> 10m (secondary), 10 -> 20m (manager)
- Use runbook links in the alert message; include dashboard and relevant log query.

Alert message template (must include):
- service, severity, symptom summary, link to dashboard, link to runbook, suggested first-step remediation.

5) Runbooks (P1 example: Control Plane API high error rate)
Title: Control Plane API - High 5xx Rate
Owner: Platform API Team On-call
Severity: P1
Symptoms:
- Dashboard shows error rate > 5% and incoming request rate is stable or rising.
- Log tail shows repeated 5xx errors with same stack trace.
- Traces show majority of errors are generated by the policy-eval component.
Immediate steps (ordered):
1. Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and notify #platform-oncall Slack channel with short summary and dashboard link.
2. Check control-plane-api pods: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=control-plane-api -o wide
3. If all pods are Ready, fetch logs: kubectl -n platform logs pod/<pod> --since=10m | grep "ERROR" | head -n 200
4. If error patterns point to a recent deploy (check image tag), roll back the canary: deployment-service rollback --service control-plane-api --to previous
5. If no recent deploy, scale replicas to reduce load impact: kubectl -n platform scale deployment control-plane-api --replicas=5
6. If the cause is downstream (e.g., policy-eval), coordinate with the owning team and enable a temporary feature-flag to bypass the failing logic.
7. Post-incident: create incident ticket, run runbook checklist, and capture timeline in postmortem template.

6) Runbooks (P2 example: Observability ingestion lag)
- Symptom: metrics ingestion lag > 2m and traces delayed > 5m.
- Quick checks: check kafka consumer lag, check storage-tier (S3/Blob) write errors, check metrics-aggregator pod restarts.
- Remediation: restart the metrics-ingestor pod, if problem persists increase consumer parallelism in deployment config, open incident if lag > 30m.

7) Retrospective: Q4 2025 - Major reliability items (summary)
- Incident: Control-plane canary rollout caused 30m outage for dedicated customer traffic (2025-11-12). Root cause: feature-flag logic change that introduced synchronous blocking call to policy-eval. Action items:
  - [DONE] New canary gating: add canary canary-traffic-shielding flag to block new code paths for >75% traffic until validated (owner: deployment-service).
  - [IN-PROGRESS] Add automated rollback if p50 latency doubles within first 3m (owner: CI/CD Team).
  - [DONE] Improve runbook notes and alert text to surface 'recent-deploy' earlier.
- Observability gap: tracing sampling disabled on some customer-facing routes leading to triage delays. Action items:
  - [IN-PROGRESS] Standardize sampling config across platform (owner: Observability).
  - [PLANNED] Backfill traces for affected windows when ingestion capacity restored.

8) Roadmap (high-level Q1-Q3 2026 priorities)
- Q1 2026:
  - Stable autoscaler 1.1: lower decision latency to p95 < 30s, support mixed instance types (owner: Platform SRE).
  - Observability upgrade: migrate to OtelCollector v2 and reduce ingestion latency to < 60s for 90% of events (owner: Observability).
- Q2 2026:
  - Deployment-service: automated gradual rollbacks and better canary scoring (owner: CI/CD).
  - Service catalog: launch internal service registry portal with ownership metadata and onboarding flow (owner: Platform Infra).
- Q3 2026:
  - Private deployment drift detection: detect and auto-suggest remediations for customer on-prem configs that diverge from supported baselines (owner: Eng Private Deployments).

9) Team wiki & operational knowledge
- Location: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki (living index). Add entries for: on-call rotation, runbook templates, Slack routing rules, escalation matrix, on-call playbook for holidays.
- On-call expectation: 30 minute response time for P1s during scheduled shifts. Primary on-call must update the incident ticket every 15 minutes until mitigated.

10) Post-incident process & retrospective template
- Immediately: create incident ticket and start timeline doc in the incident board (link in PagerDuty).
- Within 48 hours: initial incident write-up with timeline, mitigation steps, and impact.
- Within 7 days: draft postmortem with root cause, short-term mitigations, and action items owner + due dates.
- 30-day follow-up: verify action items closed or have new timelines; add to roadmap if recurring systemic issue.

11) Appendices / Quick reference
- Useful commands:
  - kubectl get events -n platform --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
  - pd incidents create --service "control-plane-api" --summary "High 5xx rate" --urgency high
- Example alert rule (Prometheus style):
  ALERT ControlPlaneHighErrorRate
  IF sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="control-plane-api",code=~"5.."}[3m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="control-plane-api"}[3m])) > 0.05
  FOR 3m
  LABELS { severity="page" }

Related links:
- Platform runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Platform roadmap (detailed): /confluence/eng-platform/roadmap
- Deployment-service docs: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/deployment-service

If anything on this page conflicts with a service-specific runbook, the service-specific runbook is the source of truth for that individual service. For platform-wide policies (alerting thresholds, paging rules, SLOs) this page is authoritative.
